heroHeadline: ASCO 2026: Daraxonrasib Nearly Doubles Pancreatic Cancer Survival; mRNA-4157 Sustains 49% Melanoma Recurrence Reduction at 5 Years
heroSubtitle: The ASCO 2026 Annual Meeting (May 29–June 2, Chicago) delivered a historically dense set of Phase 3 results. The marquee daraxonrasib (RASolute 302) Phase 3 trial nearly doubled overall survival in metastatic pancreatic cancer versus chemotherapy (HR 0.40; 13.2 vs. 6.7 months median OS) — the largest OS benefit ever demonstrated in Phase 3 PDAC, received a standing ovation at the Plenary Session, and was simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine. Adjuvant selpercatinib (LIBRETTO-432, NEJM) reduced recurrence risk by 83% in RET fusion-positive early lung cancer (EFS HR 0.172). The personalized mRNA cancer vaccine intismeran autogene sustained a 49% reduction in melanoma recurrence at 5-year follow-up (KEYNOTE-942; HR 0.51; JCO). Sacituzumab tirumotecan (OptiTROP-Lung05, The Lancet) became the first ADC + IO combination to beat pembrolizumab alone in Phase 3 first-line PD-L1+ NSCLC (HR 0.35). Ivonescimab (HARMONi-6, The Lancet) became the first China-originated drug ever selected for the ASCO Plenary in the organization's 61-year history. Abemaciclib (SARC041) delivered the first-ever positive Phase 3 result in dedifferentiated liposarcoma. Mayo Clinic validated an AI model detecting pancreatic cancer up to 3 years before clinical diagnosis on routine CT scans.
footerNote: Data sourced from FDA Drug Approvals, NIH/NCI, peer-reviewed journals (NEJM, The Lancet, JCO, Nature Medicine), ASCO/ESMO/AACR conference data, and institutional analyses. All clinical data reflect published and presented trial results.
